conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand your GJ tube came out at the nursing home. We’re going to keep you here overnight to make sure everything’s stable before replacing it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes… tube out. Hurts leg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see you mentioned leg pain. We checked your vitals and labs, and you don’t have a fever or signs of infection. Your blood work shows your white count is a bit high, but we don’t see a clear source yet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever. Just leg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor your leg. The swelling might be from lying on one side. We’ll also check your INR since you’re on warfarin for your atrial fibrillation. It was 1.9 on admission—slightly low, but we’re continuing your usual dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Warfarin okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re keeping it the same for now. Your diabetes and thyroid meds are also continuing as usual. We’re giving you pain medicine through the tube site if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We’re scheduling the GJ tube replacement today. An interventional radiologist will do it using imaging to guide the new tube into place.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They’ll use numbing medicine around the site. You shouldn’t feel much. You’ll be awake but won’t need sedation. The procedure usually goes smoothly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The team just replaced your GJ tube. It went well—no complications. The tube is in the right spot and can be used for feeding right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. Leg still swollen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We noticed that. Your right leg and arm are both swollen. Since you have a history of clots, we recommend an ultrasound to check for a DVT. It might just be from positioning, but we want to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Need it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll arrange it soon. For now, your breathing is stable, lungs are clear, and your sacral ulcer looks clean. No signs of infection at the GJ site either.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The ultrasound is pending, but we’re planning to discharge you today to extended care. Your GJ tube is working, and you’re stable otherwise.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Medicines same?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your medications continue as before. The rehab team will manage your warfarin and check your INR regularly to keep it in range.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re finalizing your discharge. Please watch for redness, swelling, or drainage at the GJ site. And the rehab team will follow up on the leg swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're welcome. You did well. The feeding tube is secure, and we’ll make sure your care continues smoothly at the facility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick update—your discharge orders are ready. You’ll go back on your regular schedule of tube feeds, medications, and monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Back to routine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Same meds, same feeds. Just make sure the rehab team checks your leg and your INR as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Understood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll have the transport team get you ready. You should be at the facility by late afternoon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Let the rehab team know if anything changes—especially with the leg or the tube site.
